source.title: SafeCOMM: A Study on Safety Degradation in Fine-Tuned Telecom Large Language Models
source.authors: Aladin Djuhera; S. Kadhe; Farhan Ahmed; Syed Zawad; F. Koch; Walid Saad; Holger Boche

record.tranche_reason: Tests benign telecom-domain fine-tuning and harmfulness rates, and reports per-token KL patterns, bearing directly on safety degradation and first-token concentration.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the reported harmfulness comparisons after telecom SFT/CPT and the three per-token KL curves described in Fig. 3. The paper also reports utility and defense results, but those do not directly measure the claim versions retained here; it does not run harmful-example fine-tuning, compliant-prefix, suffix, decoding, or safety-deepening tests.
record.test_reason: Benign telecom-domain SFT of three safety-aligned chat/instruct models. Harmfulness is measured with Llama-Guard on DirectHarm, HexPhi (the original's benchmark) and a new TeleHarm set, and per-token KL curves are reported. This is a new domain setting with results on V2 and, loosely, V3.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that benign telecom SFT noticeably degrades safety, including on telecom-specific prompts. They attribute the severe harmfulness of the CPT TeleLLMs mainly to the absence of safety samples in instruction tuning. They also conclude that lightweight defenses (SafeInstruct, SafeLoRA, SafeMERGE) restore safety with little utility cost. They read the Fig. 3 KL curves as showing alignment only a few tokens deep, and claim this is 'token-level proof' that SFT degrades safety. That claim is not established, because no pre-fine-tuning curve is shown for comparison.
record.recipe_differences: Uses benign telecom-domain SFT/CPT rather than the original study's fine-tuning recipe; evaluates telecom datasets and TeleHarm alongside DirectHarm and HexPhi, with different models and settings.
record.method_sensitivity: The magnitude of reported safety degradation differs across telecom training datasets and benchmarks; the paper says TSpecLLM has the greatest KL divergence, followed by TeleQnA and TeleData.

fits_no_version.finding: Telecom CPT models instruction-tuned on Open-Instruct, with no safety data, are highly harmful: DirectHarm about 78%, HexPhi up to 88.5%. The comparison is against the separate general instruct release.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Domain CPT from a base model followed by instruction tuning without safety data yields models with high harmful compliance.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference
record.problems: Per-token KL results are presented in a figure without numerical values. The paper gives no uncertainty estimates for the harmfulness scores and does not isolate data effects from other training differences.
record.rows_left_out: Task utility results and SafeInstruct/SafeLoRA/SafeMERGE outcome comparisons were left out because they do not directly measure the tested version outcomes retained here. Fig. 3's SafeMERGE-to-aligned comparison was also left out because it is not the aligned-versus-unaligned per-token KL comparison named by V3.

untested.parts: Only telecom QA datasets; no general benign datasets (e.g. Alpaca) and no selected benign subsets. No full-parameter fine-tuning, only LoRA.
No per-token KL for the original aligned instruct model versus base. Only Llama-3.1, only TeleHarm prompts, only 10 positions.
No prefilling, suffix or decoding attacks.
SafeLoRA/SafeMERGE adapt few layers as a defense, but localization of safety is not tested.
Causes (format, data size) are discussed but not isolated.
No training that deepens alignment beyond the first tokens. Defenses are only tested for restoring refusal rates.

record.verdict_notes: Tranche changed to T3: this is a new domain, uses a Llama-Guard judge, and is LoRA-only. The CPT rows were unlinked because those models never had safety alignment to erode. No variance or seeds are reported. The KL figure has no numeric values. Defense results were correctly left out as mitigation.

versions.untested_parts: No fine-tuning on harmful examples is reported.
The study tests telecom SFT and CPT/instruction-tuning settings, not ordinary benign datasets generally or the specific carefully selected benign examples from the claim.
Reports per-token KL on unsafe TeleHarm prompts for telecom-tuned versus unaligned Llama models; it does not provide numerical KL values or a direct aligned-versus-base comparison.
No compliant opening, adversarial suffix, or decoding intervention is tested.
Selective LoRA projection/merging is used as a defense, but the study does not test whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behaviour.
The paper discusses possible data and training explanations but does not isolate whether data or objective causes shallowness.
The defenses are not tested for spreading safety beyond the first tokens or for persistence of such deepening.
